chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Maryam al-Ansari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man fasts something from the month of Ramadan, then he does not cease to be sick until he dies, so there is nothing upon him. And if he recovers, then gets sick, then dies, and there was wealth for him, charity should be given on his behalf in place of each day by a mudd; and if there was not wealth for him, his guardian should fast on his behalf.

key_terms.مُدٍّ: A specific measure of volume (approx. 0.75-1 kg of food)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for missed fasts if a person dies after recovering and then falling ill again?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between continuous and intermittent illness to determine the method of expiation for missed Ramadan fasts, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that liability attaches only to days where the individual was capable of fasting. It establishes a dual mechanism for compensation—charity from the estate or fasting by the guardian—ensuring the spiritual debt is settled even after death. This ruling underscores the importance of the wali's role in managing the deceased's religious obligations within the Shia legal framework.
